articles.title: The Most Likely Trade For All 30 MLB Teams in 2026-27 Offseason
articles.summary: Marquee free agents like Tarik Skubal and Randy Arozarena will take center stage with the official start of Major League Baseball's 2026-27 offseason just around the bend, but trades will also feature prominently in the months until the next regular season begins.
articles.body:
Marquee free agents like Tarik Skubal and Randy Arozarena will take center stage with the official start of Major League Baseball's 2026-27 offseason just around the bend, but trades will also feature prominently in the months until the next regular season begins.

All told, there were 67 trades last offseason, including the deals that put Freddy Peralta, Mauricio Dubón, Willson Contreras, Sonny Gray, Nolan Arenado, Marcus Semien, Brandon Nimmo, Brandon Lowe and Shane Baz in their new homes.

The Rays and Red Sox led the way with 13 trades apiece. Only the Padres didn't make at least one player swap between Halloween and Opening Day.

With that in mind, we've taken an early look at what each team might be most eager to trade for/away this offseason.

While we're not proposing specific trade packages, we did include a "Prime Target" for each team that figures to do some buying.

Teams are presented in alphabetical order and broken up by division.

Estimates for 2027 arbitration-eligible salaries come from MLB Trade Rumors .

Baltimore Orioles : A Trade for a Starting Pitcher Prime Target : Seattle's Logan Gilbert (arbitration-eligible in 2027, estimated at $15.4M)

Before too much longer, Baltimore could have quite the starting rotation, led by current Double-A prospects Anthony Eyanson, Joseph Dzierwa and Caden Hunter. But the tentative plan for the 2027 rotation leaves much to be desired, needing a stopgap solution until those young'uns are ready for the show. Maybe it's Joe Ryan or Sandy Alcantara instead of Logan Gilbert, but targeting an ace-caliber arm that is one year away from free agency should be the goal here.

Boston Red Sox : A Trade for a Middle Infielder Prime Target : Houston's Jeremy Peña (arbitration-eligible in 2027, estimated at $13.1M)

Though they have a potential star waiting in the wings in the form of top prospect Franklin Arias, the Red Sox got a whole lot of nothing from their 2B and SS spots in 2026. And because they rather expect Arias to be a key piece of the puzzle by no later than 2028, trading for a multi-year solution a la CJ Abrams, Zach Neto or Corey Seager probably isn't the route they want to go, if they can instead get one year of Peña at a not-too-exorbitant cost.

New York Yankees : A Trade for a Closer Prime Target : Milwaukee's Trevor Megill (arbitration-eligible in 2027, estimated at $8.0M)

With David Bednar and darn near every other reliever of note hitting free agency, the Yankees have quite a bit of work to do on their bullpen. The dream target would be Mason Miller, if the Padres are willing to have that conversation. But while trading for Devin Williams didn't pan out how they hoped in 2025, going back to Milwaukee for Trevor Megill could be the move. He was an All-Star last year and probably ought to be a three-time reigning All-Star at this point.

Tampa Bay Rays : A Trade of Drew Rasmussen Contract : $20M club option for 2027

Most teams wouldn't dream of trading away a Cy Young caliber pitcher unless it was an unavoidable step in embracing a rebuild. Once that salary creeps north of $10M, though, it's simply a standard operating procedure for the Rays, who have dealt the likes of Tyler Glasnow, Blake Snell, Chris Archer, David Price, James Shields and Scott Kazmir in years gone by. And for an ace who was an All-Star in both 2025 and 2026, they should be able to command a return on par with what Milwaukee got for Freddy Peralta this past winter, if not better.

Toronto Blue Jays : A Trade for a Left Fielder Prime Target : Cleveland's Steven Kwan (arbitration-eligible in 2027, estimated at $11.3M)

Fourteen players made at least one appearance in left field for the Blue Jays in 2026, and they're probably going to decline their club option on the player who led the bunch with 74 appearances (Myles Straw). In theory, Anthony Santander could factor into the OF/DH mix in 2027, but Toronto almost has to view him as a fully sunk cost at this point. But like the Rays, the Guardians love to trade away players once they start getting expensive. They might be willing to move Kwan if Toronto makes it worth their while.

Chicago White Sox : A Trade for a Starting Pitcher Prime Target : Los Angeles' Reid Detmers (two years of arbitration eligibility, estimated at $7.5M in 2027)

The White Sox acquired Luis Castillo ahead of the August trade deadline, but La Piedra gave them an 8.42 ERA and hardly seems to be the answer to their pitching woes for 2027—even though they'll need to pay him $23M. A new multi-year solution would be fantastic, as they A) don't have much pitching potential in their prospect pipeline and B) never have been a big spender in free agency. Reid Detmers might be gettable from the Angels.

Cleveland Guardians : A Trade of Steven Kwan Contract : Arbitration-eligible in 2027, estimated at $11.3M

This past winter was a quiet one for the Guardians. But the previous offseason, they traded away Josh Naylor, Myles Straw and Andrés Giménez in a trio of salary dumps. They also proceeded to trade away Shane Bieber that summer, rather than risk getting stuck with his $16M player option. So, even though Kwan has been arguably a top 25 position player over the past five seasons, would anyone be the least bit surprised if they trade him away? Moving Jo Adell—projected for $9.6M in his final year of arbitration eligibility—is also very much on the table here.

Detroit Tigers : A Trade for an Established Starting Pitcher Prime Target : Texas' Jacob deGrom ($37M in 2027; $20M club option in 2028)

Detroit has quite a few viable options for its 2027 starting rotation. However, beyond Framber Valdez, it's a lot of "if he stays healthy for a change" and "might break through in 2027" types of candidates. They should have room in the budget for a big splash, though. And if they'd rather trade for one expensive year of a two-time Cy Young winner instead of trying to re-sign their former two-time Cy Young winner to what promises to be an historic contract, they should find out if the Rangers are willing to budge on deGrom, who has given them a 3.44 ERA since his arrival in 2023.

Kansas City Royals : A Trade for Relief Pitching Prime Target : Pittsburgh's Luke Weaver ($5M)

The Royals could decide to blow things up, with either one or two years of team control remaining on a bunch of core players. However, it's more likely they'll make a concerted effort to win another World Series in 2027 and/or 2028. And in order to do so, improving a bullpen that had an MLB-worst 5.10 FIP and near-worst 5.07 ERA is a must. Luke Weaver had a cup of coffee with the Royals back in 2022. Bringing him back could be a good first step.

Minnesota Twins : A Trade for a Big Bat Prime Target : Colorado's Hunter Goodman (three years of arbitration eligibility, estimated at $6.2M in 2027)

Minnesota didn't sell last winter, it didn't sell at the trade deadline and it probably isn't going to burn things down this offseason, even with Joe Ryan and Pablo López headlining a long list of key players who will be free agents one year from now. If they are, in fact, in it to win it in 2027, they need to get another potent bat into a lineup that gets mediocre in a hurry beyond Byron Buxton and Kody Clemens. Would be huge if they can get Hunter Goodman as a three-year replacement for free agent catcher Ryan Jeffers.

Athletics : A Trade of Shea Langeliers Contract : Two years of arbitration eligibility, estimated at $8.7M in 2027

Surely, the Athletics would love to have signed Shea Langeliers to the type of long-term extension with which they've locked up Jacob Wilson, Tyler Soderstrom, Lawrence Butler and Brent Rooker in recent years. However, Scott Boras doesn't play that game. And given how woeful this pitching staff is, the A's can't realistically expect to become a true contender within the next two years before he hits free agency. So, maybe trade him away now? Precious few catchers have been more valuable than Langeliers over the past three years.

Houston Astros : A Trade of One of Their Infielders Contract : See Below

Christian Walker is owed $20M next season. Houston holds a $13.4M club option on Isaac Paredes. Jeremy Peña is projected to fetch $13.1M in arbitration. All three of those infielders will be free agents next winter. But considering the Astros also still have Jose Altuve and Carlos Correa for several years to come and a dire need for starting pitching right now, there's a good chance they'll flip one of those three impending free agents, either directly for an arm or to make room in the budget to sign one.

Los Angeles Angels : A Trade of Reid Detmers Contract : Two years of arbitration eligibility, estimated at $7.5M in 2027

The sale of this franchise from Arte Moreno to Stan Kroenke gave Angels fans some hope for the first time in a long time. But do we think they're going to turn things around overnight? The year after setting a franchise record for losses in a single season? Or does the change in ownership simply mean cleaning house and finally embracing a proper rebuild for the first time? Probably the latter, and Reid Detmers would generate a lot of interest on the trade block fresh off easily the best season of his career.

Seattle Mariners : A Trade of a Starting Pitcher Contract : See Below

If Kade Anderson is here to stay (and he most likely is), Seattle enters the offseason with a six-man rotation, plus Logan Evans as a seventh option after he missed all of 2026 to an internal brace elbow surgery. Trading from that surplus to upgrade the offense could be the plan. The question is whether they sell high on Emerson Hancock (four years of team control remaining) after his breakout year, or part with Logan Gilbert, who has one year of arbitration eligibility remaining at a projected $15.4M. Our guess is the latter, as it gives them more money to play with in free agency.

Texas Rangers : A Trade for a Controllable Starting Pitcher Prime Target : New York's Luis Gil (three years of arbitration eligibility, estimated at $2.3M in 2027)

Both Nathan Eovaldi and MacKenzie Gore will be free agents next winter, while the Rangers will need to decide whether exercising a $20M club option for what will be Jacob deGrom's age-40 season is a good idea. Even ignoring that 2028 dilemma, though, they could really use another arm for 2027, as they don't have a single returning pitcher (even including that big three) who made at least six starts with a sub-4.20 ERA in 2026. The Yankees sure do have a surplus of starting pitchers, though, and would probably be willing to part with the 2024 AL Rookie of the Year.

Atlanta Braves : A Trade for a Shortstop Prime Target : Los Angeles' Zach Neto (three years of arbitration eligibility, estimated at $9.8M in 2027)

If they manage to re-sign Mauricio Dubón, never mind. Atlanta's primary trade block focus at that point would be adding a starting pitcher who might actually be able to stay healthy. As is, though, Jim Jarvis is the leader in the clubhouse for the starting shortstop gig on Opening Day, and he posted a .564 OPS before spending the final six weeks of the regular season at Triple-A Gwinnett. Dating back to July 2022, though, the Braves have made 13 trades with the Angels, and maybe they can go back to that well to snag Zach Neto.

Miami Marlins : A Trade for a Potential Closer Prime Target : Athletics' Luis Medina (three years of arbitration eligibility, estimated at $1.4M in 2027)

There's also a considerably non-zero chance the Marlins will exercise their $21M club option on Sandy Alcantara before trading him away. However, with at least two years of team control remaining on every other key contributor from this season, buying makes more sense than selling off one of the most valuable players in franchise history. And what the Marlins desperately need is a reliever to turn to in high-leverage situations. Luis Medina could be that guy, giving the A's a 3.08 ERA in his first season as a reliever.

New York Mets : A Trade for a Starting Pitcher (or a Corner Infielder) Prime Target : Minnesota's Joe Ryan (Arbitration-eligible in 2027, estimated at $9.6M)

If Bo Bichette opts out and New York uses those "savings" to get across the finish line in its impending negotiations with Tarik Skubal, trading for a corner infielder might be the way they go. But even if they do sign Skubal, the Mets could still use another starting pitcher, lest they pin their hopes and dreams on Sean Manaea and Kodai Senga again.

Philadelphia Phillies : A Trade for an Inexpensive-Yet-Impactful Outfielder Prime Target : Los Angeles' Alex Call (three years of arbitration eligibility, estimated at $1.9M in 2027)

Unless Bryce Harper is moving back to right field on a more permanent basis, Philadelphia's outfield plans for 2027 appear to be Brandon Marsh in left, Justin Crawford in center and Derek Hill in right with Bryan De La Cruz as the primary reserve. But with an estimated 2027 cash payroll that is already the highest in the majors, signing a Randy Arozarena or Ian Happ to improve that situation hardly seems like an option. Bringing Alex Call back to the NL East could work, though. He struggled in 2026, but had an .800 OPS between the 2024 and 2025 campaigns.

Washington Nationals : A Trade for a Veteran Starting Pitcher Prime Target : Kansas City's Michael Wacha ($14M in 2027, club option of $14M-$18M for 2028)

Washington's rotation is already looking more promising than it did for most of the regular season. DJ Herz, Josiah Gray and Connelly Early logged a combined total of 14.0 innings for the Nationals in 2026, but the 2027 rotation should be that trio, Cade Cavalli and Andrew Alvarez, if nothing changes. That might be the youngest rotation in the league, though, and would benefit from a veteran like Wacha, who has nearly twice as many career innings pitched (1,828) as that quintet combined (959).

Chicago Cubs : A Trade for a Starting Pitcher Prime Target : Los Angeles' Gavin Stone (three years of arbitration eligibility, estimated at $1.2M in 2027)

The Cubs have a ton of work to do on their starting rotation, but the silver lining is they should have plenty of room in the budget to make it happen. Their farm system isn't great, though, so getting one year of an ace like Logan Gilbert or Drew Rasmussen would be tough to pull off. Maybe they spend big in free agency and trade for a buy-low option like Gavin Stone? He missed all of 2025 to shoulder surgery and was unable to make it back to the big leagues in 2026, but he's a solid 'maybe' for a rotation spot in 2027 if traded.

Cincinnati Reds : A Trade of Nick Lodolo Contract : Arbitration-eligible in 2027, estimated at $5.7M

Lodolo had a rough go through 2026, hampered by a blister that kept him from making his season debut until Mother's Day weekend. But he had a sub-4.00 FIP in each of 2022, 2024 and 2025 and is a prime candidate for a bounce-back year. With only one year of team control remaining, though, the Reds might/should put him on the trade block to see how much others are willing to bet on his potential comeback campaign.

Milwaukee Brewers : A Trade of Trevor Megill Contract : Arbitration-eligible in 2027, estimated at $8M

Josh Hader. Corbin Burnes. Devin Williams. Freddy Peralta. Trevor Megill? Trading away an All-Star pitcher the year before he hits free agency has become an annual rite of passage for the Brewers. It's pretty darn hard to argue with the results, too, as they get better each year. And with Abner Uribe boasting a career ERA of 2.20 and almost certainly ready to step into the closer role—with four years of team control remaining—why wouldn't they do it again?

Pittsburgh Pirates : A Trade for a Big Infield Bat Prime Target : Houston's Isaac Paredes ($13.4M club option for 2027)

Brandon Lowe's one season with Pittsburgh was everything the Pirates could have asked for, playing in 150 games and hitting 35 home runs. Now he's a free agent, though, and it's back to the drawing board with several spots in the lineup that could use an infusion of offense. Third base, in particular, is looking bleak, and we've previously mentioned that Houston is probably going to be willing to move one of its infielders. And, come on, "Pittsburgh Paredes" is right there as an awesome nickname.

St. Louis Cardinals : A Trade for an Ace Pitcher Prime Target : Los Angeles' Reid Detmers (two years of arbitration eligibility, estimated at $7.5M in 2027)

Putting the cart before the horse here, but if the Cardinals manage to add a legitimate ace this winter, they're going to be the team that everyone falls in love with as the pick to go from sub-.500 in 2026 to a possible first-round bye in 2027. Upgrading the third base situation is presumably also on their to-do list, but adding an Opening Day starter would be huge. And they've restocked their farm system to such a degree over the past two years that they surely have the prospects necessary to make it happen.

Arizona Diamondbacks : A Trade for Relief Pitching Prime Target : Milwaukee's Trevor Megill (Arbitration-eligible in 2027, estimated at $8M)

Of their seven primary relievers in 2026, only two are slated to return. (And this wasn't a particularly good bullpen in the first place.) Maybe they pony up a big offer for free agents David Bednar or Adrián Morejón, but investing heavily in relief pitching has never really been their style. Trading for one year of a Trevor Megill or Emilio Pagan is more their speed, especially if they're not convinced Justin Martinez is the answer at closer.

Colorado Rockies : A Trade of Willi Castro Contract : $7.3M in 2027

In each of the past three years, Willi Castro has tallied at least 10 home runs, at least 10 stolen bases and at least 10 appearances at four different positions. Those types of super utilitymen who can single-handedly fill out a depth chart without needing to be hidden in the 9-hole are becoming increasingly invaluable. And it'd be a shame if another year of his prime is spent wasting away again in Colorado. He could be just what the doctor ordered for a team like Atlanta, Boston or Texas.

Los Angeles Dodgers : A Trade for a Utilityman Prime Target : Detroit's Zach McKinstry (Arbitration-eligible in 2027, estimated at $5M)

Speaking of teams who could use a super utilityman, the Dodgers need to replace the retiring Miguel Rojas, whose departure leaves their infield depth chart looking pretty shallow. Signing a Mauricio Dubón, Edmundo Sosa or Ha-Seong Kim could be the path of least resistance, but buying low on Zach McKinstry after he hit .199 in 2026 is also on the table.

San Diego Padres : A Trade for a Starting Pitcher Prime Target : Tampa Bay's Drew Rasmussen ($20M club option for 2027)

There's a dream scenario in which Michael King doesn't opt out of the two years left on his contract while both Joe Musgrove and Yu Darvish make triumphant returns in 2027. There's also a nightmare scenario in which none of those things happen and the Padres are looking at JP Sears, Jhony Brito and Jagger Haynes as regulars in the rotation behind Nick Pivetta and Randy Vásquez. In other words, there's work to be done here, and AJ Preller has never been shy about swinging big on the trade block. Maybe they can pry Rasmussen away from Tampa Bay?

San Francisco Giants : A Trade of a Big Position Player Contract Contract : See Below

The Giants still owe Rafael Devers $211M for seven more seasons, Willy Adames $140M for five more seasons, Matt Chapman $100M for four more seasons and Jung Hoo Lee $63M for three more seasons (if he doesn't opt out of his final two years next winter). Getting out from under at least one of those contracts—Chapman's would arguably be most preferable—is going to be the offseason goal for a team that has made the postseason just once in the past decade.

articles.title: Ranking Junior Caminero to Rays and MLB's 10 Most Lopsided Trades in Recent History
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays have one of baseball's brightest young stars in slugger Junior Caminero, but he could have been playing on the other side of their ALCS matchup with the Cleveland Guardians.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Rays have one of baseball's brightest young stars in slugger Junior Caminero, but he could have been playing on the other side of their ALCS matchup with the Cleveland Guardians.

The Guardians traded an 18-year-old Caminero who was still in the lower levels of the minors to the Rays for pitcher Tobias Myers on Nov. 19, 2021, in what has become one of the most lopsided trades in recent history.

What other one-sided deals make the top 10?

We've dug into the last decade of MLB trade history prior to 2026, as the dust is still settling on those deals, and ranked the 10 most lopsided trades.

To SD: OF Juan Soto, 1B Josh Bell To WAS: SS CJ Abrams, OF James Wood, LHP MacKenzie Gore, OF Robert Hassell III, RHP Jarlin Susana, 1B Luke Voit

Juan Soto joined the Padres as a bona fide superstar with two additional years of club control remaining. He helped San Diego reach the 2022 NLCS.

However, anything short of a World Series title was going to make this a lopsided trade.

CJ Abrams and James Wood have emerged as All-Stars and franchise cornerstones for the Nationals, while MacKenzie Gore developed into their de facto ace before he was flipped as the centerpiece of his own blockbuster deal.

The Padres ended up going 82-80 in 2023. They cut their losses ahead of Soto's final year of club control, trading him to the Yankees for a five-player package that included Michael King.

9. Sandy Alcantara, Zac Gallen to the Marlins

To STL: OF Marcell Ozuna To MIA: RHP Sandy Alcantara, RHP Zac Gallen, OF Magneuris Sierra, LHP Daniel Castano

This trade brought the Cardinals two productive seasons from Marcell Ozuna, who posted a 107 OPS+ while averaging 26 home runs, 89 RBI and 2.3 WAR, but they missed the playoffs in his first season and were swept in the NLCS the following year.

Since the trade, Sandy Alcantara and Zac Gallen have both logged over 1,000 innings in the majors and produced at a frontline level.

Alcantara won 2022 NL Cy Young honors and now stands as Miami's franchise leader in starts (202), strikeouts (1,074) and innings pitched (1,281.0). Gallen was flipped for Jazz Chisholm Jr. in a one-for-one swap and settled in as the ace of the D-backs staff, finishing top 10 in Cy Young voting three times and helping them reach the 2023 World Series.

To BOS: IF Vaughn Grissom To ATL: LHP Chris Sale, cash

Chris Sale pitched a total of 48.1 innings from 2020-22 before returning in 2023 with a middling 4.30 ERA over 102.2 innings, so when he was traded to the Braves, it looked like a logical salary dump that brought back an intriguing change-of-scenery candidate in Vaughn Grissom.

Sale then promptly had the best season of his career, going 18-3 with a 2.38 ERA and 225 strikeouts in 177.2 innings to win a long-awaited first Cy Young Award and the NL pitching Triple Crown. He was entering the final season of his contract at the time of the trade, but he signed a two-year, $38 million extension a few days after the trade was completed.

Grissom hit .190/.246/.219 with a negative-0.1 WAR in 31 games with the Red Sox.

A Possible Trade Made by Every Team This Offseason ⚾

To MIA: OF Lewis Brinson, OF Monte Harrison, 2B Isan Díaz, RHP Jordan Yamamoto To MIL: OF Christian Yelich

Christian Yelich was the third domino to fall during the Marlins' 2017-18 offseason fire sale, following Giancarlo Stanton and Marcell Ozuna out the door. He brought back a prospect package headlined by outfielder Lewis Brinson, who began the 2018 season as the No. 18 prospect in baseball.

A productive everyday player in Miami, Yelich immediately became one of the best players in baseball, winning NL MVP honors in 2018 and finishing runner-up in 2019 while winning the batting title both years.

His production dipped from there, but he has piled up 27.5 WAR in nine seasons in Milwaukee while earning a nine-year, $215 million extension through 2028. The four prospects who went to Miami recorded a combined negative-6.8 WAR in 581 big league games.

To LAD: RP Josh Fields To HOU: DH Yordan Alvarez

The Dodgers signed Yordan Alvarez as an amateur international free agent on June 15. Less than two months later, before he ever played a game for the organization, he was flipped to the Astros for reliever Josh Fields.

To their credit, Fields was a useful arm out of the Los Angeles bullpen over parts of three seasons, logging a 2.61 ERA over 124 appearances.

However, the Astros got one of the best offensive players in the sport. It didn't take him long to arrive, as he burst onto the scene and won the 2019 AL Rookie of the Year honors. After making a run at the AL Triple Crown this year while hitting .316/42/106, he is expected to add an AL MVP award to his trophy case.

To TB: IF Curtis Mead To PHI: LHP Cristopher Sánchez

The scales on this deal appeared to tip aggressively in the Rays' favor when Curtis Mead emerged as a consensus Top 100 prospect just a few years later, but he never quite found his footing in Tampa Bay.

On the flip side, Cristopher Sánchez was never even a top-15 prospect in the Philadelphia farm system prior to debuting in 2021. He broke through in 2023, became a full-time member of the rotation in 2024 and has put together back-to-back 8.1-WAR seasons over the last two years as one of the best pitchers in baseball.

He signed a six-year, $107 million extension that could keep him in Philadelphia through 2033. While Mead resurfaced this year with the Nationals before he was traded to the Red Sox at the deadline, there's little doubt about who won this trade.

To CLE: RHP Tobias Myers To TB: 3B Junior Caminero

Junior Caminero played 43 games for Cleveland's affiliate in the Dominican Summer League before the Rays flipped him for Tobias Myers during the 2021-22 offseason.

Myers was subsequently sent to San Francisco in exchange for cash considerations in July, with a 6.00 ERA over 14 Triple-A starts. That was the extent of his action in Cleveland.

Caminero hit .324 with 31 home runs between High-A and Double-A in 2023 to emerge as one of the top prospects in baseball. He's now working on back-to-back 40-homer seasons in the big leagues despite the fact that he is still only 23 years old.

To NYM: SS Javier Báez, RHP Trevor Williams, cash To CHC: OF Pete Crow-Armstrong

The Mets were 55-48 at the time of this trade, good for a four-game lead in the NL East standings. To his credit, Javier Báez was a terrific pickup, posting a 140 OPS+ with 18 extra-base hits and 1.7 WAR in 47 games.

However, the Mets went 22-37 the rest of the way to miss the playoffs. Báez walked in free agency that offseason and signed with the Tigers.

For what ended up being an inconsequential two-month rental, the Mets gave up presumptive 2026 NL MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong. The 24-year-old had 45 home runs, 41 steals and an NL-leading 156 OPS+ in a 9.8-WAR season. He is now the face of the franchise for the North Siders.

To CWS: RHP James Shields, cash To SD: OF Fernando Tatis Jr., RHP Erik Johnson

The White Sox signed Fernando Tatis Jr. out of the Dominican Republic for $700,000 on July 2, 2015, but he was traded to the Padres before ever making his professional debut.

With a 29-27 record at the time of the trade, the White Sox were chasing relevance, but veteran James Shields was not the answer to fortify their rotation. He logged a 6.77 ERA in 22 starts following the trade. The South Siders finished below .500 and missed the playoffs. After signing for two additional years, Shields posted a 5.31 ERA in 436 total innings in Chicago.

In eight years since breaking through into the big leagues, Fernando Tatis Jr. has tallied 31.6 WAR with three All-Star selections, two Gold Gloves and two Silver Sluggers. He has a 136 OPS+ with 177 home runs and 162 steals.

To BOS: OF Alex Verdugo, SS Jeter Downs, C Connor Wong To LAD: OF Mookie Betts, LHP David Price

Ahead of his final season under club control, and with extension talks at an impasse, the Red Sox traded homegrown superstar Mookie Betts to the Dodgers for a package built around controllable outfielder Alex Verdugo and two top prospects. They also used the deal to unload David Price's remaining contract.

In July, the Dodgers locked Betts up with a 12-year, $365 million extension. Over seven years with the team, he has piled up 36.5 WAR and won three World Series rings to solidify his status as one of the best players of his generation.

Verdugo posted a 105 OPS+ and 8.1 WAR over four seasons in Boston. He never took the next step to emerge as a star. Jeter Downs played 14 games in the majors for the Red Sox, while Connor Wong has 4.2 WAR in 425 games and remains a member of the Red Sox.

That's 12.3 WAR in exchange for a generational talent who the Red Sox never should have let get away in the first place.

articles.title: Orioles reportedly hire Cubs assistant Jared Banner as new general manager
articles.summary: Jared Banner has nearly two decades of experience around the game.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Orioles are shaking up their front office. Coming off another down year, the team decided to bring in some fresh blood, reportedly hiring Jared Banner as its new general manager, per ESPN.

Banner previously served as an assistant general manager with the Chicago Cubs.

The move comes more than a year after Baltimore's previous general manager, Mike Elias, was promoted to the team's president of baseball operations. At the time, it was reported that the Orioles would hire a new general manager ahead of the 2026 MLB season. That didn't happen, and Elias presumably filled the role in 2026.

Banner has a fairly extensive history around the game. He broke in with the Boston Red Sox, working his way from an assistant in player development to the team's vice president of player personnel in 11 years. He was then hired by the New York Mets as the team's executive director of player development. He spent two seasons with the team in that role.

After that, he joined the Cubs. Banner started out as a vice president of special projects with the team, but worked his way into an assistant general manager role. He held that position for three seasons before being hired by the Orioles on Monday.

Orioles looking for improvement after disappointing 2026

In his new role, Banner will be tasked with turning around an Orioles team that has fallen short of expectations the past two years. After going 91-71 in 2024, the Orioles have won just 75 and 79 games the past two seasons.

During that period, the team has promoted and developed a handful of promising hitting prospects, like Gunnar Henderson and Samuel Basallo. Things have lagged on the pitching side, where the Orioles have given up at least 735 runs in each of the past two seasons.
